papers.title: SALTO: Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators for Nonlinear Event Inference
papers.abstract: Learned dynamical models can accurately predict trajectories while producing unreliable sensitivities when differentiated or transposed, limiting their use in inverse problems and scientific decision-making. Classical adjoints provide exact local derivatives, but a single adjoint cannot represent the nonlinear response of a system to a family of finite-amplitude perturbations. We introduce SALTO (Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators), a Koopman-based framework for inferring finite-amplitude sources. In the lifted space, the nonlinear dynamics are approximated by a linear propagator, and its transpose carries each sensor backward in a single solve. The result is a reusable lifted adjoint that predicts the measurement produced by any candidate localized event with one encoder pass and an inner product. To give the model the simulator's exact local behavior, SALTO imposes three structural constraints: it anchors the physical-state dynamics to the simulator's linearized propagator, centers the learned observables so that they vanish to second order at the reference state, and uses a block-triangular lifted propagator. These constraints guarantee that the model reduces to the simulator's tangent dynamics and classical adjoint as the amplitude vanishes, while the learned observables carry only the finite-amplitude correction. On three nonlinear PDE systems, SALTO predicts the measurements of finite-amplitude sources to within 2-8% where the classical adjoint is in error by 41-165%, recovers source position and intensity from sparse sensors nearly as accurately as inversion through the solver, and samples the joint posterior of two interacting sources, matching the solver's posterior on reaction-diffusion at a twentieth of its cost. One trained model serves new sensor layouts and measurement times with a single backward solve.

papers.title: The role of friction on heave-induced motion of offshore drilling systems: modelling, analysis, and numerical experiments
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the influence of friction dynamics on heave-induced disturbance propagation using a coupled hydraulic-structural drilling model formulated as a semilinear interconnection of ordinary and hyperbolic partial differential equations (ODE-PDEs), and capturing spatially distributed memory effects in the drillstring-wellbore interaction. First, local and global existence and uniqueness results are established, and sufficient conditions for boundedness and input-to-state stability are deduced via a small-gain analysis. Subsequently, extensive numerical investigations are carried out, including harmonic excitation studies, nonlinear distortion analysis, spatial amplification investigations, mechanism-isolation experiments, parameter sensitivity analysis, and broadband simulations under realistic offshore sea-state excitation. The simulation results indicate that, whilst the hydraulic response is governed primarily by wave propagation phenomena, compressibility, and boundary reflections, the structural dynamics display substantially greater sensitivity to distributed friction effects. Furthermore, drillstring-wellbore friction is shown to have a relatively limited influence on well-posedness but a potentially significant impact on stability margins. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for coupled hydraulic-structural dynamics and distributed friction mechanisms when analysing, monitoring, and controlling offshore drilling systems.

papers.title: Frey-Mazur theorem for semistable elliptic curves over function fields
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a field, let $B/k$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve, and put $K=k(B)$. We prove a Frey--Mazur type theorem for nonisotrivial semistable elliptic curves over $K$. More precisely, after fixing the genus of $B$ and the characteristic of $k$, a sufficiently large prime-to-characteristic torsion representation determines the $K$-isogeny class.

papers.title: Nonpersistence of full-dimensional tori with polynomial decay in nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
papers.abstract: We establish local nonpersistence of full-dimensional invariant tori with polynomially decaying actions for the periodic quintic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \[ iu_t-u_{xx}+T_vu+\mu|u|^4u=0,\qquad x\in\mathbb T:=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z). \] For every $\kappa\geq1$, we construct a fixed bounded real Fourier multiplier $T_ve^{ijx}=v_je^{ijx}$ whose frequencies $\lambda_j=j^2+v_j$ satisfy the Bourgain-type Diophantine condition \[ \operatorname{dist}\left(\sum_j\ell_j\lambda_j,\mathbb Z\right) \geq\gamma_\kappa\prod_j(1+\ell_j^2\langle j\rangle^{2\kappa})^{-1} \] for some $\gamma_\kappa>0$ and every nonzero finitely supported integer sequence $\ell$, where $\langle j\rangle=\max\{1,|j|\}$. For this multiplier, every $3<M<4\kappa+\frac12$, every $A>0$, and all sufficiently small $\mu A^2>0$, the closed relative action tube of radius $3/10$ around $I_j=A\langle j\rangle^{-M}$ contains no full-dimensional invariant torus in $H^1(\mathbb T)$ carrying a complete flow, with arbitrary frequencies allowed. This advances the study of the polynomial-decay problem identified by Kuksin as a main open problem in KAM theory for one-dimensional Hamiltonian PDEs [Amer. Math. Soc. Transl. Ser. 2, 212 (2004), 237--258, Problem 7.1]. Bourgain discussed a related question for short-range Hamiltonian systems [Russian Math. Surveys 59 (2004), 231--246, Section 3]. The proof combines simultaneous Diophantine and weighted homological estimates, an exact common-phase transformation, and one normal-form step on four adjacent Fourier coordinates. Uniform phase rotation forces an action excursion, while overlapping parameter intervals cover all sufficiently small positive perturbations. The mechanism suggests applications to other Hamiltonian PDEs.

papers.title: Classes of integrable metrics on Banach spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce a large new class of (weak) metrics on the Hardy space that have infinite families of conservation laws in involution. The construction of the metrics and the integrals involve the Hankel operator and a field of Nijehuis operators. The commutativity of the integrals is based on the notion of the coupling transform, which allows us to recursively construct new classes of metrics and integrals. We characterize the spectrum of the Nijenhuis operators. The paper establishes a connection between a rich class of completely integrable geodesic flows appearing in the finite dimensional Riemannian geometry and a new class of integrable systems in Banach spaces.

papers.title: Emergence of partially hyperbolic skew-products with circle fibers
papers.abstract: We study the statistical behavior of partially hyperbolic skew-products over Axiom A diffeomorphisms using emergence. Generically, these systems satisfy the Palis conjecture: they have a finite number of physical measures whose basins together have full volume. In particular, for Lebesgue almost every point, the empirical measures converge to one of finitely many physical measures. We study the non-generic case and prove that, even when the sequence of empirical measures may have uncountably many accumulation points, these systems have low emergence.

papers.title: Conditional limit laws for open intermittent dynamics
papers.abstract: We obtain conditional limit theorems for open intermittent Liverani-Saussol-Vaienti (LSV) maps. Unlike the results of closed systems (e.g. some uniformly expanding maps), we obtain a new limit distribution, which is different from the Gaussian law or the stable law, for both "regular" and singular observables.

papers.title: Semisimplicity and Rigidity of the Kontsevich--Zorich Cocycle for Products of Strata
papers.abstract: We study the Kontsevich--Zorich cocycle, its fixed tensor constructions, and their finite direct sums over products of strata of Abelian differentials. The acting groups are closed subgroups $G\subset(\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R)^n$ that, up to factor permutations and coordinatewise conjugation by rotations, are products of diagonal $\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R$ blocks and a finite central group. For ergodic invariant probability measures, we prove Deligne-type semisimplicity: the bundles admit Hodge-compatible decompositions into $G$-invariant pieces $V_i\otimes_{A_i}W_i$, where $A_i$ are division algebras, $V_i$ carry pure variations of Hodge structure, and the multiplicity spaces $W_i$ carry finite direct sums of pure Hodge structures. Every invariant subbundle arises from $A_i$-submodules of the $W_i$. If block marginal measures have smooth local supports and are locally equivalent to smooth volume, Hodge-orthogonal projections onto invariant subbundles are locally polynomial in period coordinates on the normalized support. The proof obtains a local product-of-quadrics model and joint polynomiality from polynomiality along stable and unstable leaves. On the cone obtained by scaling each diagonal block together, projection coefficients admit homogeneous degree-zero expressions with integral powers of reciprocal block areas. For the full product group $(\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R)^n$, single-stratum measure classification supplies the support hypothesis, yielding rigidity for every ergodic invariant probability measure. Under the transported support hypothesis, arbitrary coordinatewise $\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R$-conjugates also admit polynomial equivariant projectors, though not necessarily Hodge-orthogonal. Genus-two examples show that nonrotational conjugation can destroy Deligne-torus invariance, and independent factor scalings can require square roots of area functions.

papers.title: Algorithms for computing basins of attraction associated with a rational self-map of the Hopf fibration based on Lyapunov exponents
papers.abstract: The objective of this work is twofold. One, we develop a theory of iteration for complex rational functions so that the problems of overflow and indeterminacy caused by null, or almost null, denominators can be avoided when developing implementations. Second, we present easily implementable methods that allow the calculation of attracting cycles as well as the graphical representation of their basins of attraction. In order to deal with our first goal, we work with homogeneous complex coordinates, and we take the complex projective line as a model, which is expressed as a quotient of the 3-sphere through the Hopf fibration. An irreducible representation of a rational function can now be presented as a Hopf fibration endomorphism. As well as our second goal is concerned, we use Lyapunov functions and exponents to calculate the cycles associated with endomorphisms and to graphically represent the corresponding basins of attraction. We point out that our algorithms are based on the calculation of a finite set of non-negative real constants, and their calculation does not depend on the previous determination of the fixed points or attracting cycles.

papers.title: Density of repelling periodic points for cubic rational maps
papers.abstract: We prove the repelling-density conjecture for cubic rational maps over $\mathbf C_p$: for every prime $p$, the classical Julia set is the closure of the classical repelling periodic points. By B\'ezivin's theorem, it suffices to prove that a nonempty classical Julia set contains a classical repelling periodic point. The case $p\geq5$ follows from known results for tame maps, so we treat residue characteristics two and three. We argue by contraposition, assuming that the map has no classical repelling periodic points. Maps with potential good reduction already have empty classical Julia set. Otherwise, we conjugate the map to an explicit normalized form and analyze its coefficients. In each case, we obtain coefficient restrictions and establish a uniform bound on the spherical derivatives of all iterates. This bound implies equicontinuity on the classical projective line and hence emptiness of the classical Julia set.

papers.title: Persistence in probability for stochastic delay equations with multiplicative noise
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic delay equation \begin{equation*} dX(t)=[-\gamma X(t)+r f(X(t-\tau))]\,dt+\sigma X(t)\,dW(t), \end{equation*} where $\gamma,r,\tau\in(0,\infty)$, $\sigma\in[0,\infty)$, and with $f$ either globally Lipschitz or globally bounded and locally Lipschitz, with $f(0)=0$ and $f(x)\ge0$ for all $x>0$. Under the condition \begin{equation*} r\liminf_{x\to 0^{+}}\frac{f(x)}{x}>\gamma+\frac{1}{2}\sigma^2, \end{equation*} independent of the time delay $\tau,$ we obtain that every solution $X$ with nonnegative initial history and $X(0)>0$ is bounded away from zero in probability. This result then confirms a recent conjecture of van den Bosch, van Gaans, and Verduyn Lunel, and yields a non-trivial invariant measure for, e.g., the Mackey--Glass or Nicholson's blowflies equation with multiplicative noise. To get to this result, we apply a transformation to the solution process, essentially rewriting the equation using a stochastic integrating factor. A comparison with a linear equation gives contraction estimates for negative conditional moments and hence boundedness away from zero in probability. The same argument yields persistence whenever the linear comparison equation has a positive first Lyapunov exponent.

papers.title: Degree Growth of Rational Maps with Laurent Property
papers.abstract: Algebraic entropy measures the exponential growth of the degrees of iterates of rational self-maps. It is introduced by Bellon and Viallet in \cite{BellonandViallet}. We study degree growth for rational maps arising from recurrences with the Laurent property, with particular emphasis on Gale--Robinson recurrences. We develop a direct method for determining the degree growth from the recurrence relation itself, reducing the problem to the study of associated max-linear, or tropical recurrences. We first obtain a closed formula for the degrees of iterates for a broad class of homogeneous quadratic Laurent recurrences. We then apply this result to the two-term Gale--Robinson family and derive an explicit quadratic growth formula with a periodic correction term. For three-term Gale--Robinson recurrences, we express the algebraic entropy in terms of the associated tropical growth rate sequence. Based on explicit computations, we formulate a conjecture for the general three-term family predicting quadratic growth with a periodic correction. We prove the conjecture for the infinite family with parameters $p=1$, $q=2$, and $r\geq3$.

papers.title: Pantograph Difference Equations: Stability, Multistability, and Chaos
papers.abstract: Pantograph equations are functional differential equations with proportional delay, typically involving terms of the form $x(at)$, where $0<a<1$. These equations have been studied for several decades and have applications in areas ranging from number theory to electrodynamics. In this work, we investigate pantograph difference equations as discrete dynamical maps of the form \[ x_{i+1}=F(x_{i})+G(x_{h(i)}), \qquad i\geq 0, \] where $h(i)\leq i$. In particular, we consider $h(i)=\lfloor ai \rfloor$ and $h(i)=\lfloor ai^{\alpha}\rfloor$, with $0<a<1$ and $0<\alpha<1$. We distinguish between homogeneous pantograph difference equations, for which $F(x)=0$, and inhomogeneous pantograph difference equations, for which $F(x)\ne 0$. We first analyze linear pantograph difference equations and establish sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability and for nonconvergence to zero. For proportional delays, analytical stability and instability regions are combined with multi-horizon parameter scans to construct regime diagrams in the $(\lambda,\delta)$-plane. We then investigate pantograph versions of the logistic and tent maps. In the homogeneous case, the dynamics evolves through step-like plateaus whose lengths increase at least exponentially, leading to slow convergence and finite-time multistability within computationally accessible time scales. In the inhomogeneous case, numerical experiments show finite-time exponential separation of nearby trajectories, consistent with chaotic dynamics.

papers.title: Uniformization of Julia sets of geometrically finite rational maps
papers.abstract: A Schottky set is the complement of a collection of disjoint open disks in the Riemann sphere. We completely characterize geometrically finite rational maps whose Julia sets are quasiconformally equivalent to Schottky sets. We also prove that the closure of the basin of infinity of a geometrically finite unicritical polynomial is quasiconformally equivalent to a Schottky set if and only if either there exists an attracting cycle and all bounded Fatou components have disjoint closures or there exists a parabolic cycle of multiplicity three. An ingredient of the proof is a new dynamical characterization of pairs of arbitrary quasicircles that are quasiconformally equivalent to pairs of tangent circles.

papers.title: On effective equidistribution for product-type self-affine measures
papers.abstract: We establish an effective equidistribution theorem on homogeneous spaces for expanding translates of product-type self-affine measures seen on unipotent orbits along any sequence of diagonal elements drifting away from walls. In particular, we do not require the diagonal elements to lie in a fixed proper and closed subcone. The main new ingredients in the proof of our equidistribution theorem include an adaptation of the methods in \cite{BHZ25} to the setting of product-type self-affine measures, as well as a weighted effective recurrence theorem for intertwined associated random walks. The latter involves decomposing the random walks according to suitable stopping times and applications of intertwined Benoist-Quint height functions.

papers.title: Strong invariance principles in deterministic systems
papers.abstract: We show that in every aperiodic, probability preserving dynamical system there is a function whose associated time series satisfies the almost sure invariance principle with rate asymptotically smaller then $\sqrt{n}$ and the almost sure weak invariance principle of Brosamler and Schatte.

papers.title: On the structure of polynomial multicorrelation sequences arising from nilpotent actions
papers.abstract: We prove that every polynomial multicorrelation sequence arising from nilpotent actions admits a decomposition into a generalized nilsequence and a null-sequence. This resolves a long-standing question of Frantzikinakis concerning the structure of polynomial multicorrelation sequences of commuting transformations. Our proof builds upon ideas underlying the norm convergence theorem of Walsh.

papers.title: An undecidable problem in dynamics
papers.abstract: Given a variety $X$ with a self-map $\phi$ and subvarieties $Y$ and $Z$ of $X$, we consider the set of $n$ for which $\phi^n(Y)$ intersects $Z$ nontrivially. Extending a beautiful construction of Lee and Nam, we show this gives rise to an undecidable problem for a fixed ambient variety $X$ and morphism $\phi$. We further use this construction to give a counterexample to a conjecture of the author, Satriano, and Sierra.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture near hyperbolic metrics
papers.abstract: We give an LLM-assisted construction of counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture, with real analytic metrics arbitrarily close to a hyperbolic metric in dimension three. For acyclic unitary line characters tending to the trivial character, the modulus of the Ruelle zeta function at zero divided by analytic torsion squared tends to zero.

papers.title: Causal Fingerprints Reveal Hidden Mechanisms in Partially-Observed Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: In partially-observed dynamical systems, distinct hidden mechanisms can produce similar observable summary statistics while explaining individual events differently. We introduce causal fingerprints: realization-dependent patterns that track how information about a hidden state is revealed through subsequent evolution. Within a prescribed dynamical model, we compare the filtering posterior, based on observations up to a given time, with the smoothing posterior, obtained after adding an expanding window of future observations. We quantify this retrospective information gain using Kullback-Leibler divergence and track its evolution as the future window of observational data expands. The fingerprint reveals both the strength and temporal reach of hidden influence, which can vary across events and their stages. Because the observed trajectory is held fixed while hidden-state inference depends on the candidate model, fingerprints reveal how competing dynamical mechanisms explain the same observations even when selected statistics agree. In linear Gaussian systems, we derive a characteristic fingerprint timescale for the temporal reach of hidden influence. Calibrated surrogates matching the observable mean, variance, and decorrelation time can still produce distinct fingerprints when feedback memory, hidden-noise memory, or hidden forcing timescales are misrepresented. Nonlinear examples reveal mechanism-dependent signatures for extreme bursts, oscillatory variability, and regime switching, including multiplicative instability versus additive forcing, deterministic nonlinear feedback versus state-dependent multiplicative noise, and intrinsic bistability versus hidden double-well forcing. Causal fingerprints therefore provide a time- and event-resolved diagnostic for asking not only whether a model reproduces observed statistics, but how its hidden dynamics explain individual events.

papers.title: Seven Limit Cycles in a Periodically Forced Three-Zone Equation
papers.abstract: We construct a seven-cycle example for a periodically forced scalar equation with a continuous three-zone piecewise-linear nonlinearity. Symbolic integration and linear elimination reduce the four-flight matching conditions to two equations in the residence times. The competing exterior visits produce an additional turn of the critical response and lead to the rational parameters $(A,B,\mu)=(9,3/2,181363/100000)$. At these parameters, finite Taylor estimates give three sign changes of the return displacement. Scalar order, analyticity along transverse itineraries, and half-period reflection then establish at least seven distinct isolated periodic orbits on the phase cylinder.

papers.title: Beyond 11/16: dense Kuramoto networks that resist synchrony
papers.abstract: How densely must a network of identical Kuramoto oscillators be wired before synchrony is its only stable state? The answer is a critical connectivity $\mu_c$ (the minimum degree divided by $n-1$), known to satisfy $11/16\le\mu_c<3/4$. We raise the lower bound from $11/16=0.6875$ to $\mu_c\ge(4+2q^*)/(7+q^*)=0.6929077\ldots$, where $q^*\approx0.6506$ is a root of an explicit polynomial of degree 8. The networks approaching this bound carry stable states that hug the four-cluster state: three neighboring clusters each split into two slightly separated halves, and the four crossed links between neighboring halves (those whose phase gap deviates most from a quarter turn) have densities approaching $q^*$. We build these networks from a coarse-grained cluster model, verify stability with interval arithmetic, and blow the model up into large networks with an exact minimum degree. The states are fragile and easily missed by numerical searches that impose stability margins.

papers.title: Critical Ising Model on the Periodic Cubic Lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}$
papers.abstract: We investigate the critical behaviour of the nearest-neighbour Ising model on the three-dimensional periodic cubic lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}$, and we present a companion set of Monte Carlo simulations. After recalling the rigorous results on the continuity of the spontaneous magnetization in $d=3$ and the triviality of the scaling limit in $d\ge 4$, we compile modern high-precision estimates of the 3D Ising critical exponents and verify the scaling relations that connect them. We then describe numerical measurements of the Binder cumulant, the magnetic susceptibility, the specific heat, the two-point correlation function, and the finite-size scaling of the magnetization. We discuss the systematic uncertainties that affect the extraction of the exponent ratios $\gamma/\nu$ and $\alpha/\nu$, and we emphasize that an exponential fit of the correlation function is not appropriate at the critical point, where the decay is algebraic.

papers.title: Minimum nonlinearity for pattern-forming Turing instability in a mathematical autocatalytic model
papers.abstract: Pattern formation is ubiquitous in nature and the mechanism widely-accepted to underlay them is based on the Turing instability, predicted by Alan Turing decades ago. This is a non-trivial mechanism that involves nonlinear interaction terms between the different species involved and transport mechanisms. We present here a mathematical analysis aiming to explore the mathematical constraints that a reaction-diffusion dynamical model should comply in order to exhibit a Turing instability. The main conclusion limits the existence of this instability to nonlinearity degrees larger or equal to three.

papers.title: Bott-integrable contact forms with large systolic ratio
papers.abstract: We show that there is no universal upper bound for the systolic ratio of Bott-integrable contact forms on closed 3-manifolds, thus providing further evidence for the relative flexibility of integrable contact forms. For the proof, we study piecewise linear approximations of Lutz forms and establish integrability of a `plug' constructed by Abbondandolo, Bramham, Hryniewicz and Salom\~ao for pushing up the systolic ratio.

papers.title: Dynamic models with $p$ parameters are identified by $2p+1$ random features
papers.abstract: A foundational principle in nonlinear dynamics is that the structure of a dynamical system can be recovered from a small number of generic measurements or coordinates. We develop an analogous principle for the identification of dynamic models for time series \textit{with noise}, which builds on previous identification results for noiseless dynamical systems. The noise is allowed to be non-iid, non-Gaussian, and dependent on the state. Our results cover noisily observed differential equations and discrete-time dynamical systems, as well as stochastic models with process noise. We illustrate the utility of this identification principle using a Lorenz-63 model and a H\'{e}non map model, both with observational noise.

papers.title: Dynamical comparison for local homeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We prove dynamical comparison for Deaconu--Renault groupoids associated to minimal surjective non-injective local homeomorphisms of compact metrizable spaces with finite Lebesgue covering dimension. As a corollary, the associated $C^*$-algebras are UCT Kirchberg algebras, recovering results by Carlsen--Thomsen via dynamical methods. In the zero-dimensional case, our result also verifies Matui's AH-conjecture for these groupoids using a recent breakthrough of Xin Li. Our proof combines techniques from both the purely infinite and stably finite regimes: We construct partial actions of non-abelian free groups as suitable ``large subgroupoids'' and establish comparison properties for these using the paradoxical towers technique developed by Gardella--Geffen--Kranz--Naryshkin. The boundary of the subgroupoid is controlled by a groupoid version of the topological small boundary property which we deduce from finite covering dimension of the unit space. As a byproduct, we prove the classical small boundary property for minimal actions of countable discrete groups on finite-dimensional compact metrizable spaces without any freeness assumption.

papers.title: Arbitrarily Fast Quantum Dispersion in Long-Range Crystals
papers.abstract: We construct the first examples of one-dimensional long-range crystals exhibiting arbitrarily fast polynomial dispersive bounds. The Floquet functions of our Hamiltonians are highly oscillatory Weierstrass functions, whose rough autosimilar structure drives the fast dispersion. The proof develops a new Fourier decay theory for $C^\alpha$ images of the Lebesgue measure, based on a Dolgopyat-inspired transfer operator method, and yields a van der Corput lemma for Weierstrass functions. As a consequence, the local time of classical Weierstrass functions of sufficiently large lacunarity exists and is $C^k$, answering a question raised by Geman and Horowitz in 1980.

papers.title: Canonical expansions of $\mathbb R_{\mathcal Q}$-germs
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ be the field of unary germs at $0^+$ definable in the quasianalytic o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ of Kaiser-Rolin-Speissegger. We construct a canonical ordered differential-field embedding of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ into the field of natural-support generalized Laurent series. Every unary germ has a unique such asymptotic expansion, and bounded germs have expansions with only nonnegative exponents. A germ admits a convergent generalized Laurent-series representation exactly when its canonical expansion converges; in that case, every convergent representation with well-ordered support is canonical. We also prove that $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ is branching in the sense of Dembner [1]. A nonresonant hyperbolic saddle with divergent Dulac series yields a bounded positive real-analytic $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$-definable germ whose canonical generalized power series diverges. This gives a negative answer to a question of Dembner asking whether every unary germ definable in a branching structure admits a convergent generalized power-series representation. Nevertheless, every bounded unary $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$-germ has a canonical formal generalized power-series expansion. Consequently, the convergent germs form a proper ordered differential subfield of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{Q}}$.

papers.title: Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images
papers.abstract: Motivated by a question of Hochman, we investigate whether two deterministic time measures or time sets can be distinguished almost surely from a single planar Brownian image. Using rescaled correlation integrals, we give a criterion for mutual singularity of the laws of the image measures, even when the time measures have the same dimension. For self-similar time sets satisfying the open set condition, we also recover the natural occupation measure from the compact image. Together, these results allow us to distinguish lattice and non-lattice self-similar sets and their natural measures within this class. For a naturally parametrised family with two contractions, with fixed dimension, each parameter can be distinguished from all but finitely many others. If the dimension is sufficiently small, every distinct parameter can be distinguished. The results are formalised in Lean.
